text:
ConocoPhillips rose slightly today, but the real story is the steep 8.4% decline over the past two weeks — driven almost entirely by collapsing oil prices. Brent crude dipped below $90 a barrel on November 10th for the first time since August, after President Trump signaled the Iran conflict could end "fairly soon," easing fears of supply disruptions. Since oil refiners and explorers make money selling crude, lower prices directly squeeze their profits and valuations.

The gap between US and global oil prices (US at $99.64 versus Brent at $107) suggests the market still sees some regional uncertainty, but the dominant trend is toward de-escalation in the Middle East and relief from the geopolitical premium that had kept prices elevated. Without that risk premium, the sector faces a headwind unless oil demand stays strong enough to support prices at current levels.
